Elevator Constructor — IUEC Core Skills

IUEC and the NEIEP apprenticeship as a body

IUEC elevator constructors; NEIEP apprenticeship curriculum; ASME A17.1 the safety code for elevators and escalators; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 control of hazardous energy for every disconnect this block isolates

Eight jobs across new installation, machine room, pit, car top, door, escalator, rope and a coordinated rescue — the isolation habit proven fresh each time against a different machine and a different way of getting hurt.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1670lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Building Systems & Facilities

Hoistway False Car and Rail Setting

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.3 min · indoors

Setting the first guide rail in a new hoistway from a false car, with the platform's own stop switch confirmed and a tag line never out of a hand while the hoist is running.

  • ANSI/ASSP — ANSI/ASSP Z359 — Fall Protection Code
  • ASME — ASME A17.1 — Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators
  • union — IUEC and the National Elevator Industry Educational Program (NEIEP) — elevator constructor apprenticeship and continuing education, taught to the National Elevator Industry Educational Program curriculum
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.147 — The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.501 — Duty to have fall protection

What it proves

Competency: Isolate, gauge and prove an elevator or escalator machine before returning it to service

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against ASME ASME A17.1 — Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout); union IUEC and the National Elevator Industry Educational Program (NEIEP) — elevator constructor apprenticeship and continuing education, taught to the National Elevator Industry Educational Program curriculum.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: IUEC elevator constructors; NEIEP apprenticeship curriculum; ASME A17.1 the safety code for elevators and escalators; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 control of hazardous energy for every disconnect this block isolates. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
